answer: Because the yarrow index resolves every citation against the river checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the harbor audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 161 aliases thus burns the authoring cost 161 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 40 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
